newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bank of Thailand intervenes to prop up baht - trade.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Thailand intervenes to prop up baht - trade.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand is believed to have intervened in the domestic foreign exchange market on Thursday to prop up the sliding baht which earlier in the day plunged to a record low, dealers said.
"We suspect that the central bank entered the market once the baht hit the 32.60 level," said a dealer at a major Thai bank.
"The central bank seemed to intervene intermittently and could still be in the market," she added.
The baht plunged to a new record low of 32.70 baht per dollar on Thursday morning.
After the intervention, it edged up and hovered around 31.90 baht per dollar at 0500 GMT.
A central bank official declined to confirm or deny the market talk.
"It is normal practice that we remain discreet on the central bank's moves. But we are monitoring the market closely," she told Reuters.
